messages:
lisa (support): quick ping — ACME reported a sudden spike of 504s to our hosted inference endpoint when sending large embed batches around 21:40 UTC. They say ~10-18% of requests in a 5m window returned 504, heavy retries in their SDK. Customer pasted sample curl + payload and some SDK logs. Opening thread for triage.

lisa (support): repro they gave (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","inputs":["...lots of items..."],"batch_size":256}'
```
They say concurrency=64 from client, retries enabled, timeout default.

chen (sre): thanks lisa. do we have edge logs for that 21:40-21:50 window? route/instance ids? any correlation id from the customer's logs?

lisa (support): customer included x-request-id header values: rqx-3f2a, rqx-3f2b, rqx-3f2c (multiple). They reported approx 21:42:10 for rqx-3f2b. I pulled a quick slice from ELB/edge — see below.

chen (sre): pasting relevant aggregator output:
```
edge-proxy-1 21:42:09 rqx-3f2b -> upstream-timeout 504 (upstream conn reset) host=up-01
edge-proxy-2 21:42:10 rqx-3f2b -> upstream-timeout 504 (no response within 30s) host=up-03
```
Pattern: intermittent upstream timeouts, not consistent 503 surge. Could be connection churn or pooling issues between edge and upstream pool.

dave (eng-runtime): two quick hypotheses: 1) NAT / ephemeral port exhaustion on our side or customer's outbound (but customer is hosted). 2) edge transparent-proxy change we flipped last week that toggles SSL passthrough vs terminate for a subset of routes — could be exposing a misconfigured keepalive or TLS session reuse bug.

max (devex): customer SDKs commonly hit this when they open many short-lived connections without keepalive. With concurrency=64 + batch_size=256 tokens that can create heavy connection churn and cause upstream queueing. Recommend quick mitigations: set concurrency=8-16, enable keepAlive: true in Node/Python SDKs, set per-request timeout to 120s and use exponential backoff (base=300ms, factor=2).

lisa (support): relaying mitigation steps to customer now. they asked for a short-term workaround while you triage.

chen (sre): can we run tcpdump on the edge frontend for that customer-routed shard for 21:40-21:45? need to check TCP FIN/RST churn and port reuse. command we can run (ops):
```
sudo tcpdump -nn -s 0 -w /tmp/edge-21-40.pcap 'host CUSTOMER_IP and port 443'
```
Also fetch conntrack stats and ephemeral port usage: `ss -s` and `cat /proc/net/ip_conntrack` (or conntrack -L).

dave (eng-runtime): I'll instrument a short debug build to log connection pool reuse metrics across the proxy -> upstream client connector. If we see a surge of 50% new sockets per second with low reuse, that points to TLS handshake overload.

max (devex): example SDK change for Node to reduce churn:
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  keepAlive: true,
  maxConcurrency: 12,
  requestTimeoutMs: 120000,
  retry: { retries: 4, minTimeout: 300 }
});
```
ask them to try with a small sample first.

status-bot: incident-note: created incident INC-2024-867 (504 spike) — assigned to eng-runtime and sre teams. Priority: P2. ETA initial triage 30m.

chen (sre): quick grep of proxy config history — we did a partial rollout of `ssl_passthrough=false` to shard-b on 2024-04-15 02:00 UTC. Need to check if this shard maps to the customer's region. I'll correlate shard mapping.

lisa (support): customer confirmed region us-west-2. that maps to shard-b per our routing table.

dave (eng-runtime): that aligns. if ssl_passthrough=false then proxy terminates TLS and re-establishes upstream TLS. If keepalive semantics differ on re-conn we could see short upstream timeouts. I'm going to revert the shard-b flag to previous behavior on canary (one instance) and observe.

dave (eng-runtime): performing a canary rollback now on edge-proxy-2. command: `./deploy --service edge-proxy --shard shard-b --image edge-proxy:v1.14.3-prev --canary 1` — will watch health.

status-bot: deploy started: edge-proxy shard-b canary rollback (deploy id dpl-7821). health checks pending.

chen (sre): while that deploy runs, collect these from the customer's SDK logs: TCP_ERR/RST count, SDK retry timing, and the exact body sizes for failed requests. also check our upstream pool logs for `tls_handshake_time` and `socket_reuse` metrics.

lisa (support): customer uploaded more logs: they show repeated `ECONNRESET` on fetch at client side just before the 504 window. Also they confirm they were sending 64 concurrent requests with no keepalive and default SDK timeouts.

max (devex): ok customer has applied our mitigation: concurrency=12 + keepAlive true + backoff. they ran for 30m and reported failed rate dropped to ~0.8% (from ~12%). good signal.

dave (eng-runtime): canary rollback finished, rolling the remainder of shard-b back now (full rollback). monitoring p95/p99 for 30m.

status-bot: deploy complete: rollback succeeded. monitoring metrics: edge-p95-latency decreased 15%, 504 count decreased 90% on shard-b.

chen (sre): post-rollback analysis: prior config caused a short-lived TLS session cache miss + new socket creation pattern under high concurrency. combined with our upstream keepalive timeout default of 20s led to more upstream handshakes and occasional queuing => occasional upstream timeouts. rollback restores previous termination semantics and keeps socket reuse higher.

lisa (support): passing final update to customer:
- root cause: edge TLS termination change increased socket churn under high client concurrency (no keepalive) -> upstream timeouts -> 504s
- mitigation (what we did): rolled back the edge change on shard-b; asked customer to enable keepalive + reduce concurrency; they applied and saw dramatic improvement
- next steps: eng-runtime to add defensive config (increase upstream keepalive, better handshake cache) and DevEx to add SDK guidance doc about concurrency/keepalive. ETA: eng-runtime PR this week, devex doc by Mon.

dave (eng-runtime): opened PR #4812 to (1) increase upstream keepalive default to 60s for terminated routes, (2) add metric for `socket_reuse_rate`. linking to PR in case notes.

max (devex): I'll draft a short KB: "Avoiding 5xx/504s: concurrency & keepalive best practices" with example patches for Node/Python/Go SDKs. Will post here when ready.

lisa (support): customer notified, they thanked us and asked to be kept in the loop when the upstream keepalive default changes. I'll follow up after PR merge.

chen (sre): closing internal triage loop for now. file follow-up tasks to eng-runtime and devex. tagging incident INC-2024-867 as monitoring -> resolved (post-mitigation). :white_check_mark: \n
lisa (support): thanks team — great cross-team response. I'll add a short postmortem entry after devex KB and eng PR land.
